sections.h2: Which Iredell County office deals with property tax?
sections.html:
Iredell County Tax Administration runs the whole property tax system from its building at 135 E. Water Street in Statesville, and it is split into an assessor division, a tax collector division and a land records mapping division. The county board of commissioners set the policy, but you deal with the staff for almost everything.

The county Tax Administration page gives weekday hours that begin at 8 a.m. and end at 5 p.m. Call 704-878-3017 for the assessor and 704-878-3020 for the collector. The mailing address is PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687.

  • Assessor division: listing, values, exemptions and appeals.
  • Tax collector division: bills, payments, delinquent accounts and closing payoffs.
  • Land records mapping: parcel maps and the online GIS used to find an owner of record.

Sellers tend to call the collector for a bill and the assessor when a value looks off.

sections.h2: What is the Iredell County property tax rate?
sections.html:
For the 2026 tax year the county levies 0.50 on every $100 of assessed value, unchanged from 2025 and 2024 on the county's chart. The budget the commissioners approved for 2026-2027 holds it there.

Your bill adds a municipal rate if you live inside a town, plus any fire or special district. The table pulls the 2026 column from the county tax rates page, each figure stated per $100 of value.

The county also bills a flat solid waste fee of $64 per household, mobile home or apartment for 2026, and half of that for an owner with the elderly or disabled exclusion. Davidson adds a $20 privilege charge on vehicles, and Mooresville has its own solid waste fee.

sections.h2: When does an Iredell County tax bill come due?
sections.html:
Statements are mailed in August with a September 1 due date, and the collector gives owners until January 5 before any charge applies. A 2 percent charge lands on January 6, followed by 0.75 percent at the start of every later month.

North Carolina law sets the same framework for every county. The listing period runs the month of January, and the statute on due dates and interest explains the January 6 trigger. A town or county may also adopt a prepayment discount, so ask the collector whether one applies to the unit you are in.

Iredell also advertises unpaid real estate taxes in the newspaper during March and adds an advertising fee to the bill. The collector lists these tools for a delinquent account:

  • Attachment of bank accounts
  • Debt set-off against state income tax refunds
  • Garnishment of wages or rents
  • Levy on rents or other money owed to you
  • Seizure of a vehicle or other personal property
  • Foreclosure

Motor vehicle tax is separate. It rides on the state tag renewal notice and is paid to the Division of Motor Vehicles, not the county office.

sections.h2: How does reappraisal work in Iredell County?
sections.html:
Iredell County reappraises every four years, which is twice as often as the state minimum of eight. The last effective date was January 1, 2023, and the county rate table says the next revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027.

The county has published an adopted schedule of values for 2027 on its assessor pages, and the commissioners have discussed preparation for the countywide reappraisal at recent meetings. State law at G.S. 105-286 sets the outside limit, and a county can choose a shorter cycle.

Appraisers group the county into neighborhoods, review recent sales in each one and adjust values to market. They screen out sales that do not reflect market value, such as transfers between relatives, gifts and trades. A sale made under pressure can also pull a price down, which is one reason the county does not rely on every closing it sees.

For a seller, a reappraisal year matters because the value on the notice becomes the base for tax bills until the next reappraisal. If you plan to list a home around a revaluation date, pull the new appraisal card from the county taxweb site before you choose an asking price.

sections.h2: What is the appeal route for an Iredell County value?
sections.html:
Iredell County sets up a ladder with three rungs, and you climb it one step at a time. The county's appeals page prints the whole sequence.

  1. Informal review: send the appeal form and your documents to the assessor at PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687, or use the online portal. The deadline is 30 days counted from the notice date, and an appraiser answers with a fresh notice that can lower, raise or keep the value.
  2. Review board: put the request in writing, naming the property and the grounds, signed by the owner or an attorney. The county's board page says to mail it and not to count on electronic filing, so confirm the method with the assessor's office at 704-878-3017. Under G.S. 105-322 the board holds its opening session in the spring window the statute sets.
  3. State commission: if the board's written decision still disagrees with you, a Property Tax Commission appeal must be filed in 30 days.

A friend or tax consultant who is not an owner or lawyer must attach a power of attorney, or the request may be rejected. At the hearing the county's appraisal starts out presumed correct, so the owner carries the proof. The county wants sales contracts, MLS data or private appraisals dated 2022, plus photos of damage and surveys.

  • Accepted reasons: the value is out of line with market on the reappraisal date, similar properties are assessed differently, or the record card has errors.
  • Rejected reasons: a big increase, inability to pay, weak county services, high taxes, or a market shift after the effective date.

sections.h2: Which state relief programs reach Iredell County homeowners?
sections.html:
Three state programs reduce the bill for a permanent residence, and a household may use only one. The assessor takes the application on the state's AV-9 form.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: for owners at least 65, or with a lasting total disability, whose 2026 income stays under $38,800. It excludes $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is greater.
  • Veteran exclusion: removes $45,000 of value for a permanent, total, service-connected disability, whatever the owner's age or income.
  • Circuit breaker: caps tax at 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for incomes up to $58,200, once the owner has spent five years in the home.

The state AV-9 notice shows the filing window stretching through June 1 ahead of the tax year. Circuit breaker savings are deferred and secured by a lien, so selling the house or moving out triggers repayment of the prior three years. Anyone in that program should obtain a payoff from the assessor before listing. Iredell also halves its solid waste fee for owners who hold the elderly exemption.

Farm and forest owners can apply for present-use value, and builders can claim inventory relief, both through the same division.

sections.h2: How does a sale in Iredell County change who owes the tax?
sections.html:
A house that sells after January 1 leaves the seller on the hook for that year's bill, because ownership is fixed on that date. Dividing it with the buyer is a private arrangement worked out at closing.

The collector says a transfer does not release the seller, that the bill for the transfer year still goes to the seller, and that any proration is a contract matter. Questions about how it was divided go to your realtor or closing attorney. If you want no loose ends, you can request that the payment be made to the collector at closing, and the office will take a prepayment based on the previous year's rate if the current bill is not out yet.

Unpaid back taxes are the sharper risk. A tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355, so the buyer's lawyer will want the account paid up. The county advertises the owner of record as of the delinquency date, which is another reason to get a payoff figure before a contract is signed.

sections.h2: How large and how expensive is Iredell County?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts estimates Iredell County's population at 211,798 for mid-2025, a 13.5 percent jump over the 2020 count base. Its land area is 574.41 square miles, and it holds about 93,711 housing units.

  • Owners live in 71.9 percent of occupied homes (2020-2024)
  • Typical home value among owners: $321,400
  • Household income at the median: $81,419
  • Rent at the median: $1,252 a month
  • Permits issued for new building during 2025: 1,835

The county includes Statesville, Mooresville, Troutman, Davidson, Harmony and Love Valley, and each taxes at its own rate on top of the county's. Commuters average 25.1 minutes to work.

faqs.q: What is the Iredell County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is .50 per $100 for 2026, and Statesville, Mooresville and other towns add their own rates. Check the county rates page for your town and fire district.

faqs.q: When must Iredell County taxes be paid?
faqs.a: Bills are due September 1 and are penalty free through January 5. Interest of 2 percent starts January 6, then 0.75 percent more each month.

faqs.q: Where do I file an appeal in Iredell County?
faqs.a: File first with the assessor at PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687, within 30 days of your value notice. If that fails, a written appeal goes to the county review board, and the last stop is the state Property Tax Commission.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when I sell in Iredell County?
faqs.a: The seller is billed for the year of sale if the house sells after January 1, and proration with the buyer is settled in the contract or at closing. You can ask to pay the collector at closing.

faqs.q: Does Iredell County offer relief for older homeowners?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners aged 65 and over, or disabled, may qualify for the elderly or disabled exclusion when income is within the limit, and applications are taken through June 1. The county also halves the solid waste fee for those owners.
